Now we use the IP of the speaker as `unique_id`.

issue_context.title: KEF LS50 entity duplicated upon HASS start if the speakers device is offline
issue_context.body: ### The problem Every time I restart Home Assistant the entity for KEF LS50 speakers gets duplicated if the speakers are turned off at the moment. It works fine if the speakers are on. This is the very first edition of KEF LS50 Wireless that does not support wake-up over ethernet. ### What is version of Home Assistant Core has the issue? core-2021.3.3 ### What was the last working version of Home Assistant Core? _No response_ ### What type of installation are you running? Home Assistant Core ### Integration causing the issue KEF ### Link to integration documentation on our website https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/kef/ ### Example YAML snippet ```yaml media_player: - platform: kef host: 10.0.1.32 type: LSX name: kef_bedroom - platform: kef host: 10.0.1.33 type: LS50 name: kef_living_room supports_on: false ``` ### Anything in the logs that might be useful for us? _No response_ In case if the speakers are off (offline) after HASS restart I get two entities `media_player.kef_living_room` and `media_player.kef_living_room_2`. I also have KEF LSX and those work just fine, I assume that's because they are always online.

<sub><sup>(message by IssueLinks)</sup></sub>
@basnijholt I noticed you actively contributed to this integration recently. Thank you for the great support! Please take a look at this issue if you got a moment. Thank you again!

Hey there @basnijholt, mind taking a look at this issue as its been labeled with an integration (`kef`) you are listed as a [codeowner](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/dev/CODEOWNERS#L244) for? Thanks!
<sub><sup>(message by CodeOwnersMention)</sup></sub>

@basnijholt I have the same issue with my KEF LSX' (when I restart Home Assistant, not on a reboot of the host system). The original entity will become unavailable and a new entity (in my case media_player.kef_lsx_2) will be created.

@eugenet8k I fixed the issue with a workaround. It's caused by the integration that's unable to get the MAC address of the speakers. The MAC address is used as a unique identifier and when restarting I think it's able to get a MAC address. In that case there are two different unique ID's and a duplicate entity will be created. In order to fix this, you need to open /config/.storage/core.entity_registry and find the **duplicated** KEF media_player entity (probable something like media_player.kef_2). Copy the unique_id line. Find the **original** entity (something like media_player.kef) and replace the unique_id line with the line you just copied. Remove the duplicate entry from the file, save and restart the server. This should fix it.

@tobiebooth thanks for the hint. I usually got this issue resolved by turning on the speakers and then restarting the HomeAssistant service. Usually, the entities get in order (the duplicated one removed, and the proper one becomes active). But that's annoying because if I at least once restart HA when the speakers are off, I need to do another restart with speakers on. So not sure if manually editing of entities as you suggested needed at all.

There hasn't been any activity on this issue recently. Due to the high number of incoming GitHub notifications, we have to clean some of the old issues, as many of them have already been resolved with the latest updates.
Please make sure to update to the latest Home Assistant version and check if that solves the issue. Let us know if that works for you by adding a comment 👍
This issue has now been marked as stale and will be closed if no further activity occurs. Thank you for your contributions.

This is still an issue, just didn't have the time to investigate yet.

I did also notice this myself now actually.

@basnijholt yeah, it's very relevant, it only relates to the older KEF LS50 that go to full network offline mode while turned off. Now every time I need to restart the HASS server (config update or other maintenance), I will go to my room and turn on my speakers to keep them online while I deal with HASS, which prevents creating these entity duplicates. So there is a workaround, despite being generally annoying.

I believe this is because of 
https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/f17a5f0db93d696442d9144e9064089d37e088db/homeassistant/components/kef/media_player.py#L124-L141

where we use the MAC address as `unique_id`. When the speaker is offline, the mac address will return as None.

I am testing using the IP as `unique_id` instead locally. If this works well, then I will create a PR that should finally fix this issue.

I recommend using my code from here https://github.com/basnijholt/home-assistant-config/tree/master/custom_components/kef_custom.

It implements a fix, however, this code change is not acceptable to be in core (see this PR https://github.com/home-assistant/core/pull/52902).

@basnijholt thanks for the try, I guess I could switch to a custom component, but that's a hassle in the long run as well. I was curious if we could just allow setting unique id from the configuration.yaml to skip the mac address resolver.

Hi @basnijholt @eugenet8k may I ask, I have a very similar issue and I'm not sure if its related to the exact same underlying problem around unique IDs. I also have an older firmware version of the LS50 Wireless so am trying to use a Harmony Hub IR signal to switch them on/off, triggered from a 'Script'. As part of experimenting with this and also the power button on the kef integration on the dashboard, I noticed a few errors appearing in the logs.

2021-10-13 21:54:11 WARNING (MainThread) [homeassistant.helpers.entity] Entity media_player.kef_2 is incorrectly being triggered for updates while it is disabled. This is a bug in the kef integration

This happens if the speakers are off and I tried (of course it shouldn't work) to switch them on from the home assistant UI. What happens is, I then manually switch them on, but in the background, the python script seems to be retrying? to send the power toggle signal. It then turns the speakers off, but this repeats, I switch them on, and the integration again switches them off haha. Its like it has queued up lots of retried toggle signals, or has timed some of them out but they are still there somehow.

I then disabled the kef entity in the UI temporarily but the logs are indicating what I thought, the kef integration is still there running trying to do things. Is it all related to a similar issue with unique ids when powered off? My issue is not having multiple entities appear, now I cannot reactivate the entity, it does not appear on the dashboard at all, even after rebooting the home integration. Very strange.

I would be more than happy to contribute to this repo as I have been working with python for 10+ years, just might need some pointers as to where to start.

@mark007 from your case, as you admitted you can't turn on the KEF speakers with older firmware, but only via IR.  But it seems you still have a case when you send home assistant (not IR) "switch on" event for the offline speakers. I might assume that the home assistant puts that into a queue and then applies it once the speakers become online. The fix that @basnijholt just applied to the latest home assistant v2021.10.4 just ensures that the home assistant wouldn't create duplicated entries for offline speakers (at the moment of hass start) and it works. But I assume because speakers are set into a "not ready" state somehow the events that are sent to them might be queued up. 

Long story short, it seems you will be fine by ensuring you do not send any events to the speakers if they are offline (unavailable). I do similar automation to sync my TV and Speakers states. Usually, when the TV gets on I send an IR signal to turn speakers on and if TV gets off, I sent a home assistant event to turn off speakers and it works just fine.

Thanks so much for your reply. @eugenet8k I just completed a very similar set up last night that I am quite pleased with. I had a case where multiple changes of scene within a 30 second window would cause my speaker on/off state to get mixed up and from the source of the Kef integration and it's dependencies that the fastest it can detect the speaker state is about 30 seconds. Lowering this would really help with things going out of sync. I changed the interval of the Kef integration to lower values than the 30 default but there are other timeouts hard wired into the python that mean 30 seconds is really the fastest you can guarantee to be aware of state changes.

I used a ping binary to ping the speakers every 4 seconds and it seems to help here. I can detect the speaker off state in about 7 or 8 seconds and the on state takes about 16 seconds. It'd be a nice improvement to the integration to at least allow the poll interval to be reduced and remove any hard coded higher timeouts in the underlying python.

What do you guys think. Maybe not a discussion for this ticket.
@mark007 you might want to create another KEF issue with a request to add configurable poll interval settings?
Thank you. Done. https://github.com/home-assistant/core/issues/57691

Hi guys, what is the proposal for this particular issue. I see a proposed fix was not merged into the core. I am constantly getting extra devices like kef_2 created, so its breaking all scripts/automations that interact with the kef integration. For this reason its really unusable for me as it makes this integration too unreliable (while away from home this weekend, it again switched from kef to kef_2 so the rest of the family were in panic mode as no automations were working :) )

@mark007 I think the fix was merged and I confirmed at my setup that the duplicated entity is not being created anymore if you restart Home Assistant while KEF speakers are offline. I am at Home Assistant 2021.10.4.

review_comments:
it is not allowed to use the host or IP for the unique IDs, see:

<https://developers.home-assistant.io/docs/entity_registry_index/#unacceptable-sources-for-a-unique-id>
Do you have another suggestion? The examples wouldn't work, so should I use the `config_entry_id`?

<https://developers.home-assistant.io/docs/entity_registry_index/#unique-id-of-last-resort>

Yes, however, in that case, we can migrate existing entities on entry setup so it won't be a breaking change.

I cannot find a single example that uses `async_setup_platform` and `CONF_ID` in some way.

How can I get the Config Entry ID?

Oh right, this is a platform component with unique IDs. That is a fairly rare combination, especially without using config entries.

In that case, the unique ID of last resort doesn't apply, sorry.

Any other ideas?

I am looking at https://developers.home-assistant.io/docs/entity_registry_index/#example-acceptable-sources-for-a-unique-id but do not see any that would apply.
Migrate the integration to use a config flow, as that provides a config entry of which the ID of that entry can be used.

Unfortunately, I won't have time for that any time soon.

In the meantime, this PR is solving a real problem people are having.

Would you know a simpler solution for the time being?
We cannot accept the current suggested solution and if the possible solutions aren't implemented right now; There is not a real other solution imho.
What should be done with this PR at this point @basnijholt ?
If there is no option at all to fix this without completely transferring to a config_flow, then we should close this PR. I do not see that I will have the time to do that in the near future.
@basnijholt would it be possible to allow setting the arbitrary unique ID from the configuration.yaml? So if it is provided by a user then the mac address resolution would be skipped.

> would it be possible to allow setting the arbitrary unique ID from the configuration.yaml? 

That is only allowed for integrations that are out of scope for ADR-0010, unfortunately, for this integration ADR-0010 does apply.

> If there is no option at all to fix this without completely transferring to a config_flow, then we should close this PR

I'm not aware of the information the KEF integration provides, if nothing more than this then indeed a closing of this seems inevitable at this point in time.

An alternative is that if the device is offline, you raise `PlatformNotReady`. In that case it will be automatically retried later. In the meanwhile an `unavailable` entity will be automatically created.
That is a great idea, thanks Paulus. I will do that!
Thanks, I have implemented that suggestion in  #56508.
